gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a one-cable, driver-free feed to two or three added screens depends on DisplayPort MST, and macOS mirrors MST displays instead of extending them, so on a Mac only an extender with a display driver (such as FOPO's UsbDisplay) or one with a video-capable cable per screen gives separate screens.
standout_why: I opened the UPERFECT guide (cited in chat 2), which says base M1/M2 MacBooks 'only support one external display' and that its BE14BF needs a driver for one-cable use, but it never mentions MST or that one-cable driver-free screens mirror on a Mac. I also opened Dealectric's own 16-inch page (cited in chat 2): it covers driver vs native video, the UsbDisplay HDCP trade-off, cost per added screen and weight per added screen, but not MST mirroring. The Newegg Hyangin Z3 page (cited in both chats) returned 403, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answers only say 'one-cable setup with a required driver' and 'MacBook compatibility also varies by chip'.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. A 'one cable' claim tells a Mac owner nothing until the maker names the video path. On a Mac, the FOPO S11 (native, one USB-C or HDMI cable per screen, no driver, fits 12–18.5-inch laptops per FOPO) extends both screens when the Mac can drive two external displays. The FOPO S788 (driver required) is the route for base-chip Macs, at the cost of the HDCP issue. The size label barely matters: 1920×1200 is 148 ppi at 15.3 inches, 145 at 15.6 and 141.5 at 16, about 4.6% apart. So a 15-inch shopper should not rule out the 16-inch FOPO rows for sharpness; whether they fit is a question of the maker's stated fit range.

findings.source_title: Understanding MST: Multi-Display Setups with Windows, macOS, and DisplayPort (Plugable)
findings.note: Quote: 'MST-connected displays are mirrored, not extended.' Plugable is a named dock maker. This is what makes 'one cable, no driver, Mac compatible' an incomplete claim for two or three added screens.

findings.value: Native USB-C or HDMI plus USB power, no driver; fits 12–18.5-inch laptops (FOPO's range); 2 × 16-inch 1920×1200

findings.label: Video path
findings.value: UsbDisplay driver required; USB-C or dual-head USB-A to USB-C; external PD power; 3 × 16-inch 1920×1200 (laptop + 3 = 4 displays)
findings.source_title: Best triple-screen laptop extender for a 16-inch laptop with 1920×1200 panels (2026) · Dealectric
findings.note: This is the one-cable route that does extend on a Mac. Our page records that allowing UsbDisplay under Screen Recording disables HDCP, so protected video may not play. FOPO's own physical fit range for it is 12–18.5 inches (our product record).

findings.label: Pixel density of 1920×1200 by stated diagonal
findings.source_title: Best triple-screen laptop extender for a 16-inch laptop with 1920×1200 panels (2026) · Dealectric
findings.note: Arithmetic: sqrt(1920² + 1200²) = 2,264.2 px diagonal, divided by each maker's stated diagonal. 15.3 in is the FOPO S980 listing, 15.6 in is the Hyangin Z3 listing title, 16 in is the FOPO S11/S9G/S788. Panel width at 16:10 is 0.848 × diagonal: 13.0 in at 15.3 in, 13.6 in at 16 in. The 15.3-inch and 16-inch panels differ by about 4.6% in linear size and sharpness.
